mainTopic: בלעם and the moment of ה׳'s anger, רב יוסף's rule about davening מוסף on ראש השנה, and רבי יהושע בן לוי's teachings on מצוות and תשובה.
overview: The גמרא asks how בלעם could "know the knowledge of the Most High" when he could not even read his own donkey's mind, and it tells the story of the donkey shaming him. It explains that בלעם only knew how to catch the exact moment of ה׳'s anger, and that ה׳'s kindness was not getting angry at all in those days. The גמרא then says the anger lasts only a רגע and comes in the first three hours of the day, when a rooster's crest turns fully white. רבי יהושע בן לוי once tried to use that moment to curse a heretic, fell asleep, and learned that cursing people is not proper. רב יוסף rules that a יחיד should not daven מוסף early on the first day of ראש השנה, and the גמרא defends his rule against several challenges. Next comes a series of sayings from רבי יהושע בן לוי: this world is for doing מצוות, and in עולם הבא those מצוות testify for ישראל and strike the nations. Finally, he teaches that the עגל happened to give hope to בעלי תשובה, supported by רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. The question of why דוד and ישראל sinned is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: How could בלעם know God's mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that בלעם "knows the knowledge of the Most High" and challenges the simple reading: a man who did not understand his own donkey could not know God's mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says בלעם "knows the knowledge of the Most High." Is that possible? He did not even know what his own animal was thinking. Could he really know what God was thinking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about בלעם and attacks its simple meaning with a rhetorical question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק says בלעם understood God's thoughts. The גמרא argues that this cannot be what it means, because בלעם failed to understand even his own donkey. So the words must mean something smaller and more specific.

keyTerms.meaning: The knowledge (mind) of the Most High, meaning God
Is it possible? Here it is a rhetorical question meaning "it can't be"
Did he really know? (said with doubt)

phrases.english: "And knows the knowledge of the Most High"

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר דַּעַת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ לָא הֲוָה יָדַע,
phrases.english: Is it possible that he did not know the mind of his animal,
and yet he knew the mind of the Most High?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפְשָׁר דַּעַת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ לָא הֲוָה יָדַע
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of "וְיֹדֵעַ דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן" as full knowledge of God's mind
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who could not read his own donkey's mind certainly could not read God's mind.

steps.title: What does it mean that he didn't know his animal's mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that בלעם did not understand his own donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do we mean when we say "he did not know the mind of his animal"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain the claim it just used. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 1 depends on the idea that בלעם did not understand his donkey. Before going on, the גמרא wants to show this from the story in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: What is meant by "he did not know the mind of his animal"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the claim used in the challenge
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we see that בלעם did not understand his donkey?

steps.title: The princes mock בלעם and the donkey speaks up
steps.stepSummary: The princes ask בלעם why he rides a donkey and not a horse. He lies that his horse is out grazing. The donkey answers that it is his regular donkey. He tries to cover up by saying he uses it only for loads.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the princes saw בלעם riding a donkey, they asked why he wasn't riding a horse. He said, "I left it out in the pasture." Right away the donkey said, "Am I not your donkey?" He answered, "Only for carrying loads."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer with a story. בלעם is embarrassed in front of the princes, and his own donkey shows that his excuse is false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלעם wanted to look important, so he claimed he owned a horse. He never expected his donkey to contradict him. Not seeing this coming is what it means that he "did not know his animal's mind."

keyTerms.meaning: A horse, the more honorable animal to ride

phrases.english: At the time that they saw him
phrases.notes: "They" are the princes of מואב who were traveling with him.

phrases.english: that he was riding on his donkey,
they said to him: What is the reason
that you do not ride on a horse?
He said to them: I left it out in a meadow.
phrases.notes: Literally, "I threw it into the moist grass." He means the horse is out grazing.

phrases.english: Immediately: "And the donkey said,
Am I not your donkey?"
He said to it: Only for carrying loads.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעִידָּנָא דַּחֲזוֹ לֵיהּ דַּהֲוָה רְכִיב אַחֲמָרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by telling the story
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בלעם lied that he had a horse and did not expect his donkey to expose him.

steps.title: The donkey keeps exposing בלעם
steps.stepSummary: Each time בלעם tries to cover up, the donkey quotes more of the פסוק against him. It ends by saying it serves him by day for riding and by night as a wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The donkey said, "You have ridden on me!" He said, "Only once in a while." The donkey said, "Your whole life until today! And not only that, I serve you for riding by day and as a wife by night."
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. The donkey answers each excuse until בלעם is completely shamed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the words of the פסוק as the donkey's replies to בלעם's excuses. "Upon which you have ridden" answers "only for loads." "All your life" answers "only once in a while." Then the donkey reveals something even worse about him.

keyTerms.meaning: By chance, once in a while

phrases.english: It said to him: "Upon which you have ridden!"
He said to it: Only once in a while.
It said to him: "All your life until this day,"
and not only that, but
I serve you for riding by day
and as a wife by night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the donkey's replies
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The donkey shamed בלעם completely, including revealing his improper behavior.

steps.title: A source for the hint about the night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows from a word in the פסוק that the donkey was hinting at relations. It compares "הסכנתי" to "סוכנת," which is used about אבישג and דוד המלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says "הַהַסְכֵּן הִסְכַּנְתִּי," and there it says "and let her be a סֹכֶנֶת (companion) to him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from the פסוקים for the last line of the donkey's speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The donkey's words use the root ס-כ-ן. The same root appears in the word for אבישג, who was brought to be close to דוד. Because the same word is used in both places, the donkey's word is read as hinting at closeness at night too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here… and it is written there (linking two פסוקים through a shared word)
I was accustomed, from the root ס-כ-ן

phrases.english: It is written here: "Was I ever accustomed (hahasken hiskanti)"
and it is written there: "And let her be a companion (sokhenet) to him."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:2, about אבישג and דוד המלך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the donkey's last claim from the פסוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared root ס-כ-ן in במדבר 22:30 and מלכים א 1:2

steps.title: What בלעם really knew: the moment of God's anger
steps.stepSummary: Since בלעם could not know God's mind, the גמרא explains the פסוק to mean only that he knew how to pinpoint the exact moment when הקדוש ברוך הוא is angry.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what does "knows the knowledge of the Most High" mean? He knew how to find the exact moment when הקדוש ברוך הוא is angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its first question and gives the real meaning of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 1 ruled out the idea that בלעם understood God's thoughts. Now the פסוק is narrowed to one small skill: knowing the timing of God's anger. That fits a person who otherwise lacked understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (bringing a new explanation after the old one was rejected)

steps.whatToRemember: בלעם did not know God's thoughts. He only knew how to catch the exact moment of God's anger.

phrases.english: Rather, what does "and knows the knowledge of the Most High" mean?
That he knew how to pinpoint that moment
at which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is angry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the original question after finishing the donkey story
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בלעם knew the precise moment of God's anger.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן" means only knowing the timing of God's anger.

steps.title: Support from the נביא מיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects this idea to the פסוק in מיכה, where the נביא tells the Jewish people to remember what בלק planned and what בלעם answered, so they will know God's kindnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the נביא told them: "My people, remember what בלק king of מואב planned, and what בלעם son of בעור answered him, from שיטים to הגלגל, so that you will know the righteous acts of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that fits the new explanation of בלעם's power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls what happened with בלעם one of God's "righteous acts" toward the Jewish people. This fits the idea that בלעם had a real danger to offer, the moment of anger, and that God's kindness kept it from harming them.

phrases.english: And this is what the prophet said to them:
"My people, remember now
what Balak, king of Moab, planned

phrases.aramaic: וּמֶה עָנָה אוֹתוֹ בִּלְעָם בֶּן בְּעוֹר
phrases.english: and what Balaam son of Beor answered him,
from Shittim to Gilgal,
so that you may know the righteous acts of the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation that בלעם knew the moment of God's anger
steps.raayaObject: That בלעם's danger was his knowledge of the moment of God's anger

steps.title: ה׳'s kindness was not getting angry in those days
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the kindness mentioned in מיכה was that ה׳ did not get angry at all during the days of בלעם. Had He gotten angry, ישראל would have been destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: ה׳ told ישראל, 'My nation, see how many kindnesses I did for you. I did not get angry at you all those days. If I had gotten angry, nothing would have been left of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains what the 'kindnesses of ה׳' in the פסוק in מיכה were. ה׳ held back His anger during the whole time בלעם was trying to curse ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said בלעם's only power was knowing the exact moment of ה׳'s anger. רבי אלעזר adds that ה׳ simply did not get angry during those days, so בלעם had no moment to use. That is the kindness ישראל is told to remember.

keyTerms.meaning: The enemies of ישראל, a polite way of saying ישראל itself
A survivor or an escapee, meaning anyone at all left over

steps.confusionAlert: 'The enemies of ישראל' here really means ישראל itself. The גמרא avoids saying something bad directly about the Jewish people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:
My nation, see how many kindnesses
I did for you
that I did not get angry at you
during all those days,
for if I had gotten angry at you,
there would not have remained of the enemies of Israel
phrases.notes: This is a polite way to say ישראל itself. The גמרא doesn't want to say outright that ישראל would be wiped out.

phrases.english: a single survivor or escapee.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר לָהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the 'kindnesses of ה׳' in the פסוק from מיכה (Step 7) were.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s kindness was that He held back all anger during the days of בלעם, so בלעם's curse had nothing to work with.

steps.title: בלעם himself admits he cannot curse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that בלעם's own words to בלק match רבי אלעזר: he could not curse, because ה׳ was not angry.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what בלעם told בלק: 'How can I curse when God has not cursed? How can I be angry when ה׳ is not angry?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי אלעזר with a פסוק where בלעם himself says he is stuck. ה׳ is not angry, so he has nothing to work with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא זעם ה׳' line up exactly with רבי אלעזר's point that ה׳ did not get angry in those days. The proof comes from the mouth of בלעם, the one who wanted to curse.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he meant when he said
I will be angry at, I will curse in anger

phrases.english: And this is what Balaam said to Balak:
"How can I curse whom God has not cursed?
And how can I be angry at whom ה׳ has not been angry?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's statement with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ did not get angry during the days of בלעם

steps.title: How long does ה׳'s anger last
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long ה׳'s anger lasts and answers: one moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long does His anger last? A moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question: if בלעם was looking for ה׳'s angry moment, how long is that moment? The short answer is 'a רגע'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why בלעם needed exact timing: the anger is so short that only someone who knew the precise instant could use it. This answer sets up the next question about how long a רגע is.

phrases.english: And how long does His anger last?
A moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Branches off from the idea of ה׳'s moment of anger to ask how long it lasts.

steps.title: A moment is as long as saying the word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a רגע is. אמימר (or רבינא) answers: as long as it takes to say the word 'רגע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long is a moment? אמימר, and some say רבינא, said: as long as it takes to say 'רגע'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down how long a 'moment' is. The answer is tiny: just the time it takes to say the word itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the anger lasts a רגע, which is vague. Here it is given an exact, very short length. This makes clear how hard it would be for anyone to catch that moment.

phrases.english: And how long is a moment?
Ameimar said, and some say it was Ravina:
A moment is as long as saying it.
phrases.notes: He means as long as it takes to say the word רֶגַע out loud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'moment' mentioned in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: As long as it takes to say the word רגע

steps.title: A פסוק shows the anger is only a moment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that ה׳'s anger lasts only a moment and brings a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know His anger is only a moment? Because it says: 'His anger is for a moment; life is in His favor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the claim in Step 10 and brings a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק directly links 'רגע' with 'באפו' (His anger). It also contrasts that short anger with a lifetime of ה׳'s favor.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that His anger lasts a moment?
As it is written:
"For His anger is for a moment; life is in His favor."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for Step 10's claim.
steps.raayaObject: ה׳'s anger lasts only a moment

steps.title: A second source from ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another פסוק as the source: 'Hide for a brief moment until the anger passes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can learn it from here: 'Hide for a brief moment, until the anger passes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second option for the source, a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק teaches the same point another way: anger passes after only a 'brief moment'. Both sources reach the same conclusion; this is simply another way to show it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (another option)

phrases.english: And if you want, say it is learned from here:
"Hide for a brief moment
until the anger passes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, alternate source for the same idea as Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: ה׳'s anger lasts only a moment

steps.title: When ה׳'s anger happens: the rooster sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when ה׳ is angry. אביי answers: within the first three hours of the day, when the rooster's crest turns white.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is He angry? אביי said: in the first three hours of the day, when the rooster's crest turns white.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know how long the anger lasts, the גמרא asks when it happens. אביי gives the time range and a sign to recognize it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי gives two pieces of information: a general window (the first three hours of the day) and a visible sign (the rooster's crest turning white). The sign is how one could tell the exact moment within those hours.

phrases.english: When is He angry?
Abaye said:
During the first three hours (of the day),
when the crest of the rooster turns white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the length of the anger, asks about its timing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When ה׳'s moment of anger happens
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the first three hours of the day, when the rooster's crest turns white

steps.title: But the crest is white every hour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's sign: the rooster's crest is white at every hour, so how can it mark a special moment?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it turns white every single hour!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's sign. If the crest is white all the time, it can't point to one special moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sign is only useful if it shows up at one particular time. If the crest whitens every hour, it cannot tell you when the anger moment is.

phrases.english: But every single hour it is white!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sign אביי gave in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's sign of the white rooster crest
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sign that appears every hour cannot point to one specific moment.

steps.title: The difference is the red streaks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: at other hours the white crest still has red streaks, but at the moment of anger it has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every other hour there are red streaks in it; at that hour there are no red streaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The sign is not just 'white' but completely white, with no red streaks at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crest is whitish all day, but usually some red lines remain. Only at the moment of ה׳'s anger does it become fully white, so the sign does point to one specific moment.
steps.whatToRemember: ה׳'s anger lasts only a רגע, as long as it takes to say the word. It comes in the first three hours of the day, and the sign is a rooster's crest that turns fully white with no red streaks.

phrases.aramaic: כָּל שַׁעְתָּא אִית בֵּיהּ סוּרְיָיקֵי סוּמָּקֵי,
phrases.english: Every other hour there are red streaks in it,

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא שַׁעְתָּא לֵית בֵּיהּ סוּרְיָיקֵי סוּמָּקֵי.
phrases.english: but at that hour there are no red streaks in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל שַׁעְתָּא אִית בֵּיהּ סוּרְיָיקֵי סוּמָּקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refining the sign: complete whiteness rather than general whiteness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sign is just a white crest, which happens all the time
steps.terutzMaskana: The sign is a crest with no red streaks at all, which happens only at the moment of anger

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי tries to curse a heretic
steps.stepSummary: A heretic kept bothering רבי יהושע בן לוי. He set a rooster by his bed to catch the moment of anger and curse him, but when the moment came he dozed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain heretic kept bothering רבי יהושע בן לוי with questions on פסוקים. One day he took a rooster, put it between the legs of his bed, and watched it. He thought: 'When that moment comes, I will curse him.' When the moment came, he dozed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that puts the rooster sign into practice. רבי יהושע בן לוי tries to use ה׳'s moment of anger against a heretic, but falls asleep right when it arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like בלעם, someone tries to use the moment of anger to curse, and again it does not work. The story continues past this point, where the גמרא will explain what רבי יהושע בן לוי learned from falling asleep.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי הֲוָה מְצַעֵר לֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was being bothered by
a certain heretic [with questions on verses].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: One day he took a rooster
[and placed it between the legs of the bed],
and watched it.

phrases.aramaic: סְבַר: כִּי מָטָא הָהִיא שַׁעְתָּא אֶלְטֵיהּ,
phrases.english: He thought: When that moment comes, I will curse him.
When that moment came, he dozed off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי הֲוָה מְצַעֵר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story that uses the rooster sign described in Steps 14 and 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע בן לוי tried to use the moment of anger to curse the heretic, but fell asleep when it came. The lesson is drawn in the continuation.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי learns not to curse
steps.stepSummary: After dozing off, רבי יהושע בן לוי concludes that cursing people is not proper, and he backs this up with two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Learn from this that it is not proper to do this. It is written, 'And His mercies are on all His works,' and it is written, 'Punishing, even for a righteous person, is not good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the last step ends. רבי יהושע בן לוי understands that falling asleep was a message from Heaven: he should not have tried to curse the heretic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He brings two sources. The first shows that ה׳'s mercy covers everyone, even sinners. The second shows that causing someone to be punished is not good, even when a צדיק does it.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude
Proper conduct, the right way to act

steps.whatToRemember: Even when someone is wicked and causing trouble, a צדיק should not try to bring a curse or punishment on him. ה׳'s mercy covers all His creations.

phrases.english: He said: Learn from this
that it is not proper conduct to do this,
phrases.notes: "This" means trying to curse the heretic at the moment of ה׳'s anger.

phrases.english: "And His mercies are on all His works" is written,
phrases.notes: תהלים 145:9. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and it is written: "Punishing, even for a righteous person, is not good."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְמִיעְבַּד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the story in step 17
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is not proper to curse people, even wicked ones, because ה׳'s mercy is on all His works and punishing others is not good.

steps.title: What causes ה׳'s anger in the morning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי מאיר teaches that ה׳ becomes angry when kings put on their crowns and bow to the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: At the time when the kings place their crowns on their heads and bow down to the sun, הקדוש ברוך הוא immediately becomes angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ה׳'s anger comes in the morning. That is when kings get dressed in their crowns and bow to the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the anger comes in the first three hours of the day. This ברייתא gives the reason: idol worship by kings happens at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the name of

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
At the time when the kings place their crowns on their heads
and bow down to the sun,
immediately the Holy One, Blessed be He, becomes angry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the morning time of anger described in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s anger is triggered when kings crown themselves and bow to the sun in the morning.

steps.title: Do not daven מוסף alone early on the first day of ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that an individual should not daven מוסף in the first three hours of the first day of ראש השנה, because he may be judged strictly and rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A person should not pray מוסף during the first three hours of the day, on the first day of ראש השנה, when praying alone. Since judgment is being taken into account then, perhaps they will examine his deeds and he will be pushed away and rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a practical rule based on the idea that the early morning is a time of strict judgment. Someone davening alone should wait before saying מוסף on the first day of ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ראש השנה the whole world is being judged. If a person stands alone in that strict time, Heaven may look closely at his deeds and turn away his תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: ראש השנה, the start of the year
Judgment is being taken into account
He is pushed away or rejected

steps.whyThisMatters: This takes the אגדה about ה׳'s anger and turns it into a practical guideline about davening.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A person should not pray the Mussaf prayer
during the first three hours of the day
on the first day of Rosh Hashanah, as an individual,
since judgment is being taken into account,
perhaps they will examine his deeds
and push him away, and he will be rejected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the idea of a strict morning time of judgment to davening on ראש השנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual should not daven מוסף in the first three hours of the first day of ראש השנה.

steps.title: Why not the community too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if that time is dangerous, a צבור should also not daven מוסף then.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the community too should not pray then!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף. If the early hours are a time of strict judgment, why limit the rule to an individual?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's reason, strict judgment, seems to apply to everyone. So the rule should cover a צבור as well.

phrases.english: If so, the community's prayer too should not be said then!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit of רב יוסף's rule to an individual
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's limit of the rule to a יחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason given, strict judgment, applies to a צבור as well, so the rule should too.

steps.title: The community has great merit
steps.stepSummary: A צבור is not rejected, because its merit is great.
steps.simpleTranslation: The community's merit is great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: a צבור is protected even in a time of strict judgment, because its combined merit is large.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual is judged on his own deeds. A group's merit together is strong enough that its תפילה is not pushed away.

phrases.english: The community's merit is great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between an individual and a community
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Strict judgment should endanger anyone who davens at that time.
steps.terutzMaskana: A צבור's great merit protects its תפילה, so only a יחיד is at risk.

steps.title: Why not an individual's שחרית too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if an individual is at risk then, he should also not daven שחרית in those hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, an individual's morning prayer should also not be said then!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge. שחרית is also said in the first three hours, so why does רב יוסף speak only about מוסף?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a יחיד is in danger of being rejected during those hours, the danger should apply to any תפילה he says then, including שחרית.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, דְּיָחִיד דְּצַפְרָא נָמֵי לָא!
phrases.english: If so, an individual's morning prayer should also not be said!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, דְּיָחִיד דְּצַפְרָא נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge on רב יוסף's rule, after the first was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's limit of the rule to מוסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שחרית is also said in the first three hours, so the same danger should apply.

steps.title: Communities are davening שחרית at the same time
steps.stepSummary: An individual's שחרית is not rejected, because communities are davening שחרית at that same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is a community praying at that time, he is not rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: when a יחיד says שחרית, communities everywhere are saying it too, so his תפילה joins theirs and is not pushed away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The individual is protected by the merit of the צבור praying at the same moment. This is why רב יוסף's rule is only about מוסף.

phrases.english: Since there is a community that is praying,
he is not rejected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any תפילה of a יחיד in those hours should be at risk.
steps.terutzMaskana: During שחרית a יחיד is joined by communities davening at the same time, so only his מוסף is at risk.

steps.title: Isn't ה׳ learning Torah in the first three hours?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: we said earlier that in the first three hours ה׳ sits and learns תורה, not that He judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say: In the first three hours הקדוש ברוך הוא sits and engages in תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to an earlier teaching that seems to contradict רב יוסף. If the first three hours are for תורה, why would judgment be strict then?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's rule assumes judgment happens in the first three hours. The earlier teaching about ה׳'s day placed תורה in those hours, so the timing seems wrong.

phrases.english: But didn't you say:
phrases.notes: This points back to the teaching on דף ג עמוד ב about how ה׳ spends each set of three hours in the day.

phrases.english: During the first three hours, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
sits and engages in Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ: שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge on רב יוסף, this time from an earlier teaching
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's assumption that judgment happens in the first three hours
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier teaching said the first three hours are for תורה, not judgment.

steps.title: Reverse the order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the earlier teaching should be reversed: judgment comes in the first three hours, and תורה after that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by flipping the order in the earlier teaching. That way judgment is in the first three hours, which fits רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of dropping רב יוסף's rule, the גמרא changes the order in the other teaching. Judgment now falls in the first three hours, matching the morning time of anger from step 14.
steps.whatToRemember: An individual should not daven מוסף in the first three hours of the first day of ראש השנה. A צבור is protected by its merit, and an individual's שחרית is protected by communities davening at the same time.

phrases.english: Reverse it.
phrases.notes: Switch the order in the earlier teaching, so the first three hours are for judgment and the next three are for תורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the order of an earlier teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first three hours are for תורה, so judgment is not strict then.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order is flipped: judgment comes in the first three hours, which supports רב יוסף.

steps.title: Keep the order: during תורה hours there is no going beyond the law
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: do not reverse the order. תורה is called 'truth', so while הקב״ה learns תורה He does not go beyond the strict law. In judgment He can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: don't reverse anything. The תורה is called 'truth' (משלי: 'Buy truth and do not sell it'), so during that time הקב״ה does not go beyond the letter of the law. Judgment is not called 'truth', so there He can go beyond the letter of the law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer the challenge from step 25, without flipping the order of the hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the answer was to switch the order. Here the order stays: תורה first, judgment later. The danger for an individual in the first three hours is that תורה means strict truth, with no room for extra mercy. During judgment hours הקב״ה can act with mercy, beyond what the law strictly requires.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (a second answer)
Beyond the letter of the law, giving more mercy than strictly required

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'judgment' is the harsh time here. In this answer, the time of תורה is the strict time, and judgment is where mercy can come in.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Actually, do not reverse it;
the Torah, about which "truth" is written,
as it is written: "Buy truth and do not sell it"
the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not act
beyond the letter of the law;
judgment, about which "truth" is not written,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, acts
beyond the letter of the law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the challenge of step 25, as an alternative to the reversal in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of why the first three hours are dangerous, keeping the original order
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since judgment comes later, the first three hours (תורה) should carry no risk for an individual.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה hours are hours of strict truth with no extra mercy, so an individual is still at risk then.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming sayings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a short memory list (today, testifies, strikes, the calf) for the series of sayings from רבי יהושע בן לוי that follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: Today, testifies, strikes, the calf.)
steps.whatsHappening: This line is just a memory aid. It sets up the next group of sayings so a learner can remember their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one saying: 'today' (do מצוות today), 'testifies' (מצוות testify), 'strikes' (מצוות strike the nations), and 'the calf' (a saying about the golden calf that comes later). It adds no new law.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a short list of key words

phrases.english: (Today, testifies, strikes, the calf: a memory aid.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion about the hours of the day and opens a new set of teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory list for four teachings of רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: Today is for doing מצוות, and reward comes later
steps.stepSummary: Returning to a saying quoted earlier, רבי יהושע בן לוי explains 'today to do them': this world is for doing מצוות, not for getting their reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the saying itself. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What does the פסוק mean, 'which I command you today to do them'? Today is the time to do them, not tomorrow. Today is the time to do them, not today to receive their reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a saying it mentioned earlier and now explains it fully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'today' is read as 'this world'. It teaches two things. The chance to do מצוות is only in this world, not in עולם הבא. And the reward is not paid in this world but saved for עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: going back to explain a saying quoted earlier

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic idea for the next sayings: what we do in this world gets its full payoff in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Which I command you today, to do them"?
"Today to do them":
and not tomorrow to do them;
phrases.notes: 'Today' means this world and 'tomorrow' means עולם הבא.

phrases.english: "Today to do them":
and not today to receive their reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first of the sayings listed in the memory aid ('today').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This world is the time to do מצוות; their reward is given in עולם הבא.

steps.title: מצוות will testify for Israel in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that the מצוות Israel does will come as witnesses for them in עולם הבא. He reads a פסוק in ישעיהו to show it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: All the מצוות Israel does in this world will come and testify for them in עולם הבא. As it says: 'Let them bring their witnesses and be justified; let them hear and say: It is true.' The first half is about Israel; the second half is about the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second saying in the memory list ('testifies'): the מצוות act as witnesses for Israel in the World to Come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is split in two. Israel brings witnesses (their מצוות) and is found right. The nations hear this testimony and admit, 'It is true.'

keyTerms.meaning: And they will be found right, justified

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִצְוֹת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: All the מצוות that Israel performs in this world
come and testify for them in the World to Come,
as it is said:
"Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified,
let them hear and say: It is true."
"Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified":
these are Israel;
"let them hear and say: It is true":
these are the nations of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל מִצְוֹת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second saying in the memory list, building on the idea that reward comes in עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel's מצוות serve as witnesses on their behalf in עולם הבא, and the nations admit the truth.

steps.title: מצוות will strike the faces of the nations in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that Israel's מצוות will strike the faces of the nations in עולם הבא. He learns it from the word 'in the eyes of' (rather than 'before') the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: All the מצוות Israel does in this world will come and strike the nations of the world on their faces in עולם הבא. As it says: 'Guard and do them, for this is your wisdom and understanding in the eyes of the nations.' It doesn't say 'before the nations' but 'in the eyes of the nations.' This teaches that the מצוות will strike the nations right in their faces in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third saying in the memory list ('strikes'): the מצוות will come up against the nations directly, in their faces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from an exact choice of words. The פסוק could have said 'before the nations', meaning simply in front of them. Instead it says 'in the eyes of the nations', which suggests something hitting them right in the face.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the nations, in front of them
In the eyes of the nations

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי's sayings form one picture: this world is for doing מצוות. In עולם הבא those מצוות speak for Israel as witnesses, and they stand against the nations, striking them in the face.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִצְוֹת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: All the מצוות that Israel performs in this world
come and strike the nations of the world
in the World to Come, on their faces,
as it is said: "Guard them and do them,
for this is your wisdom and your understanding
in the eyes of the nations."
It does not say "before the nations,"
but rather "in the eyes of the nations,"
which teaches that they come and strike

phrases.aramaic: לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם עַל פְּנֵיהֶם לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: the nations of the world on their faces in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל מִצְוֹת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third saying in the memory list, parallel in form to step 30 but about the nations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israel's מצוות will stand against the nations in עולם הבא, striking them in the face, as learned from 'in the eyes of the nations'.

steps.title: The calf was made to give hope to those who repent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says Israel made the עגל only so that בעלי תשובה would have something to point to. His proof is the פסוק where ה׳ praises Israel's heart at that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Israel only made the calf in order to give an argument to people who repent. As it says: 'Who would give that they had this heart, to fear Me all the days.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth saying from the memory list in step 28 ('the calf'). רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that the sin of the עגל had a hidden purpose: to give hope to people doing תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that right after מתן תורה‎, ה׳ described Israel's heart as one that fears Him. People on that level would not normally fall into such a big sin. So the sin must have been allowed to happen for a purpose: to show that even a huge sin can be forgiven.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'an opening of the mouth'; an argument or claim someone can make
'Who would give'; a way of saying 'if only'

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע בן לוי is not saying the עגל was not a sin. He is saying that people on Israel's level should not have fallen so low, so the fall must have had a purpose.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Israel did not make the calf
except to give an argument
to those who repent,
as it is said:
"Who would give that they had this heart
to fear Me all the days, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: לֹא עָשׂוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הָעֵגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next saying in the series of רבי יהושע בן לוי, matching 'the calf' in the memory list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sin of the עגל happened to show בעלי תשובה that repentance works even for a great sin.

steps.title: Neither David nor Israel was fit for their sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support from רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: דוד was not fit for his sin, and Israel was not fit for the עגל. A פסוק is given for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this matches what רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: דוד was not fit for that act, and ישראל was not fit for that act. דוד was not fit, as it is written: 'And my heart is hollow within me.' And ישראל was not fit, as it is written: 'Who would give that they had this heart, to fear Me all the days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יהושע בן לוי's idea matches an older teaching from רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. That teaching says both דוד and Israel were on too high a level to commit the sins they did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For דוד, the פסוק 'my heart is hollow within me' shows his heart was empty of the pull to sin. For Israel, the same פסוק from step 32 shows their heart was full of fear of ה׳. Both sins should not have happened, which sets up the question of why they did.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is'; this matches what someone else said

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
David was not fit for that act,
phrases.notes: 'That act' for דוד is the sin with בת שבע; for Israel it is the calf.

phrases.english: and Israel was not fit for that act.
David was not fit for that act,
as it is written: "And my heart is hollow within me,"
and Israel was not fit for that act,
as it is written:
"Who would give that they had this heart
to fear Me all the days,"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 32 by showing an earlier teaching that says the same thing.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's claim that Israel was too high to have made the עגל on their own level.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's teaching, with פסוקים from תהלים and דברים.

steps.title: So why did they sin?
steps.stepSummary: Since neither דוד nor Israel was fit for their sins, the גמרא asks why they did them. The answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why did they do it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks the obvious question and is preparing the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both דוד and Israel were on such a high level, their sins need an explanation. The question opens the door for the answer, which will connect back to helping בעלי תשובה.

phrases.english: So why did they do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 33: if they were not fit for these sins, why did they commit them?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason דוד and Israel sinned even though they were not fit for those sins.
